page.layout: One printed title page, one block of text, set centred. Upper part: title lines in large capitals. Middle: verse lines in roman and italic. Lower part: a rule, a Latin motto line, a short verse block, the imprint and date at the foot. No margin notes. The scan is partly upside down and shows show-through.

main_text.l: To help mend his Native Country, la-
mentably cattered, both in the upper-Leather
and helping all the broken shoes he can make [?].
And as willing never to bee paid for his worke,
It is his Trade to patch all leather long, Gratis [?].
Therefore I pray Gentlemen keep your purses.
Whatsoever a man sayes are tormented to the Ladies,
Coblers must their awles upon the heeles.
Thus with three to feare [?] Sutor, [?] greene,
Printed by John Dow [?] for Stephen Bowtell at the great Bible in Popes Head Alley, 1647.

page.notes: Scan is rotated; several lines are upside down or mirrored by show-through and are read with doubt. Lines marked [illegible] or [?] are uncertain. The Latin motto line and the verse lines in the lower half are only partly legible. The engraved or ornamental device at the left of the lower block is not transcribed.
